To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Aquatic macrophytes do not accumulate Gd from GBCA-s, and they do not remove GBCA-s from water in low or medium concentrations.

(i) the uptake and release of Gd from aquatic macrophytes is not significant; (ii) the uptake of Gd is concentration dependent and is significantly higher in C demersum; (iii) Gd uptake is higher in Omniscan-treated macrophytes than in Dotarem-treated ones.

(1) aquatic plants are not efficient biofilters for Gd, (2) the tissue concentration of GBCAs is higher in C. demersum than in Lemna gibba and (3) there is a significant difference in tissue Gd concentration in plants treated with open-chain and macrocyclic ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of aquatic macrophytes to be biofilters for GBCA-s.
the question whether the aquatic macrophytes could be used for the removal of GBCAs from the water.
the biofiltration of Gd in water and its uptake and release in aquatic macrophytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GBCA-s are not bioaccumulated by aquatic macrophyte species, but their uptake and release is species specific.
the use of macrophytes as a biological filter in constructed wetlands to remove gadolinium-based contrast agents is not recommended.
the use of aquatic plants in constructed wetlands is not recommended for GBCA removal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gd uptake and its release from the macrophytes were concentration-dependent and the uptake and release rates were different for the two GBCA-s.
aquatic macrophytes are not suitable for the removal of GBCAs from water.
aquatic macrophytes are not biofilters for GBCA-s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aquatic plants are unlikely to be used as biofilters for GBCA-s.
GBCAs are not bioaccumulated by aquatic plants and therefore they are not a significant threat to aquatic food chains.
the GBCA-s are not bioaccumulated by aquatic plants.
